chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from 'Isa ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “For the mu'adhdhin, in the period between the adhan and the iqamah, there is the like of the reward of the martyr who is drenched in his blood in the way of Allah.”
He said: “I said, O Messenger of Allah, they compete eagerly for the adhan.”
He said: “No. There will come upon the people a time when they will cast the adhan upon their weak ones, and those are bodies whose flesh Allah has forbidden to the Fire.”

key_terms.الشَّهِيدِ: the martyr slain in the way of Allah
key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the call announcing the time of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the second call immediately preceding the prayer
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنِ: the one who gives the call to prayer
key_terms.ضُعَفَائِهِمْ: their weak or socially disregarded people
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the path and cause of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of the mu'adhdhin between the adhan and iqamah in hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the immense reward of the mu'adhdhin during the time between the adhan and the iqamah, likening it to the reward of a martyr in the path of Allah. It also foretells a time when people will leave this duty to their weak ones, while affirming the spiritual rank and protection of those who perform it.
